subject: Tidewater discovery — deployment topology, SLO targets, and test plan
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Chris Park <chris@tidewater.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Tidewater discovery — deployment topology, SLO targets, and test plan

Hi Chris / Priya,

Thanks again for squeezing us in this morning — really useful conversation. Below is a concise recap of the areas we agreed on during the call plus the technical asks we committed to follow up on. I tried to separate customer goals from constraints so we can move quickly to a PoC scope and an initial SOW draft.

High-level goals (Tidewater):
- Sub-200ms p95 response for chat-style assist flows under steady-state traffic (expected baseline 60 QPS)
- Support both short-form (<=128 tokens) and long-form (up to 2048 tokens) generations without model correctness regressions
- Keep inference cost within X budgeting constraints (you mentioned 30% reduction target vs current provider)

Primary constraints / risks we heard:
- On-prem data residency requirement for PHI workflows in Q4 (customer prefers Private deployment for PHI)
- Bursty daytime traffic with sustained 45–75 QPS and peaks up to 200 QPS for short windows
- Procurement requires an initial security package (SOC2 + data flow diagram) and a separate MSA review by their legal team

Technical recap / proposed starting topology:
- Model: prefer open LLM for tuning — you flagged Mistral-instruct / Llama-70B family as potential fits. We'll prepare two variant profiles: 1) Mistral-instruct (8-bit quantized) for cost-first evaluation, 2) Llama-70B-4bit for quality-focused scenario.
- Serving topology: Dedicated pool for production (reserved), Private control plane for PHI. Start PoC in hosted sandbox region (us-west) to run throughput/latency sweeps; then evaluate Dedicated sizing for predictable p95 targets.
- Caching/batching: plan to enable prefix/KV cache for the long-form flows and continuous micro-batching for high-QPS short flows. Expect ~20–30% token-cost reduction from cache for your typical conversation patterns.
- Fallbacks/routing: canary to smaller quantized variant (Llama-70B-4bit -> 4-bit quant) for capacity pressure with automatic degradation metrics tied to correctness evals.

Concrete asks / next steps (what I'll do):
1) Attach a short PoC checklist and recommended test payloads (see tidewater_poc_requirements.xlsx). Please confirm acceptance criteria for the PoC (latency p95, throughput, model quality thresholds).
2) Provide an initial Dedicated sizing sketch and predicted unit cost ranges for both model variants by EOD Tuesday.
3) Share SOC2 evidence bundle and a data flow diagram (we'll put a Private deployment checklist together).

What we need from Tidewater to scope the PoC:
- Representative request traces / token distribution (anonymized) — you mentioned you could provide a day of traffic sample
- A short list of 8–12 prompts/scenarios for quality evaluation (particularly for the long-form summarization flow)
- Preferred test window dates for load test (you suggested mid-Oct)

Attachments: [Attachment: tidewater_poc_requirements.xlsx (Spreadsheet, 48KB)]
References: [Attachment: redwood-deploy-topology-v1.pdf]

If that aligns, I'll pull Connor in to run a sizing/throughput simulation and Jordan will schedule the engineering deep-dive next week.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad

Subject: Re: Tidewater discovery — deployment topology, SLO targets, and test plan

Mina — thanks for the thorough write-up. This matches what we discussed and is very actionable. A couple clarifications from our side:

- PoC acceptance criteria: aim for <=180ms p95 for short-flow (<=128 tokens) at 75 QPS sustained, and <=300ms p95 for long-flow (avg 700 tokens) under 20 QPS. We'll provide a formal list of prompts by Friday.
- Data sample: PRD team will anonymize and send a day of traces tomorrow (we'll redact user ids).
- Legal/procurement: procurement@tidewater.ai looped in — they want an initial pricing range for the Dedicated commit options (monthly and annual) plus preferred cancellation terms.

Also: we have a hard requirement that PHI-bearing traffic be isolated to a private deployment before any model fine-tuning is attempted. Sandbox PoC can be hosted.

We'll take a look at the attachments; thanks for including the topology sketch. One question for your infra team: do you support multi-region read replicas for KV caches or is the cache local to the serving boundary? At scale we worry about cross-region tail latency.

Chris
VP Product | Tidewater AI
chris@tidewater.ai

Thanks — looping in our infra sizing doc and an availability window.

Quick answers and confirmations:
- KV cache behavior: Redwood's KV cache is local to the serving boundary by default (per-region). For multi-region read patterns we recommend either: 1) regional read replicas with async warm-up (best for low cross-region tail latency), or 2) a fronting routing layer that pins PHI traffic to the Private region and routes global low-sensitivity traffic to the nearest region. Jordan, I'll sync with you on the one-pager details.

- Sizing sims: attached is a short sim summary (we'll upload full sim outputs to the shared drive). Early read: Mistral-instruct (8-bit) looks like it meets the short-flow p95 at ~75 QPS on a 4x A100 pool with micro-batching tuned; Llama-70B-4bit needs 6x A100s to hit comparable p95 under the same traffic profile but yields better long-form quality. We'll show token-cost estimates for monthly vs annual committed capacity.

- Next steps: I can run a 2-hour load sweep in your sandbox next Wed (2026-10-20) 10:00–12:00 PT if that works for your infra team. Also prepping a short runbook for canary fallback to quantized variants during the PoC.
